A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoDy/GreeDy research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and renamed policies and relocated results can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original TGN explanation experiments, including fidelity, sparsity, runtime, search-iteration effects, and explanation similarities in Section 5 and Appendices C–G.

after.justification: v2 retains original TGN experiments and additionally reports TGAT results, PGExplainer comparisons, and parameter sensitivity experiments in its main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The greedy and MCTS procedures, four selection policies, and fallback strategy are retained. Event-impact renames local-gradient. Normalizing the default search weights from (2,1) to (2/3,1/3) preserves their relative weighting. Expanded pseudocode documents existing components without establishing a procedural redesign.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate future-link explanations on UCI-Messages, UCI-Forums, and Wikipedia, separating correct and incorrect predictions. Publishing previously omitted TGAT results adds model-specific evidence, not another dataset, task, or population.

E2.justification: PGExplainer is newly evaluated in the TGN comparisons in v2 Tables 1 and 4; v1 explicitly excluded it. T-GNNExplainer and the GreeDy variants remain. TempME remains unevaluated, and the newly discussed GRACIE is not an experimental comparator.

E3.justification: v2 makes AUFSC+ and AUFSC- primary metrics, integrating fidelity with explanation sparsity. It also corrects the reported fidelity- definition from one minus prediction agreement to agreement. Added protocols include PGExplainer at fixed sparsity 0.2 and controlled sensitivity settings for alpha and candidate-set size; the main CoDy search budget remains unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds a focused sensitivity study on TGAT/UCI-Messages, varying the exploration–exploitation balance and candidate-set size. The earlier runtime, search-iteration, and Jaccard-similarity analyses are largely retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable empirical uncertainty estimates. The added results retain descriptive reporting without introducing an uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds AUFSC results, PGExplainer scores, complete TGAT results, and sensitivity findings. For example, TGAT/UCI-Messages correct-prediction fidelity+ is 0.38 for GreeDy-spatio-temporal versus 0.32 for CoDy-spatio-temporal. All 216 existing TGN values in v1 Table 2 are retained in v2 Table 4; the new metrics do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix D corrects the mathematical definition of fidelity-, resolving its conflict with the stated sufficiency interpretation. Appendix F.2 adds a model-call complexity argument: O(itmax), or O(itmax + N) for event-impact with N candidates. No substantial theorem or proof development is added.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces the claim of up to 59% higher counterfactual-discovery success with 16% improvement in AUFSC+ over the strongest baseline. This changes the headline performance claim to a sparsity-aware criterion while retaining the central contribution of counterfactual explanations for TGNNs.

C2.justification: v2 adds practical guidance on choosing spatio-temporal policies without ground-truth labels, proposes possible early-stopping and hybrid-search options, and identifies user studies as future validation. Its TGAT and sensitivity discussions connect weaker results to search configuration. The original limitation to removal-based explanations remains.

D1.justification: v2 supplies detailed CoDy subroutines, node attributes, and score updates in Appendix B, specifies the neighborhood-depth rule and characterization weights, and newly reports CPU, GPU, and memory specifications. It replaces the anonymous code location with a named GitHub repository. However, v1's explicit 30-epoch training and early-stopping description is omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds substantive discussion of GRACIE and explains why its discrete-time formulation does not transfer directly to continuous-time graphs. It also adds generative-explainer and MCTS references while trimming broader background citations. The central positioning around counterfactual explanations for CTDG-based TGNNs remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methodology, results discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. v2 separates the evaluation framework, adds practical considerations, and reorganizes appendices around algorithm details, target models, and sensitivity analysis. Terminology changes include local-gradient becoming event-impact.

P2.justification: v2 adds a factual-versus-counterfactual illustration, redraws the CoDy framework, retypesets algorithms, and introduces a differently structured main AUFSC table. The original results table moves to the appendix; TGAT and sensitivity displays are added, while the fidelity+/fidelity- scatter display is removed. Several existing plots are resized or redisplayed.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves the paper's evidential support and reproducibility through previously omitted TGAT results, detailed CoDy procedures, controlled sensitivity evidence, and correction of the sufficiency definition. These address important gaps in v1. Reporting remains imperfect: TGAT Table 3 includes char=0.03 for fidelity values 0.19 and 0.50, inconsistent with its formula, and explicit training-duration details disappear. These defects temper, but do not outweigh, the substantial gains.
